newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - German DAX index tops 3,000 for first time.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - German DAX index tops 3,000 for first time.

text.p: Germany's 30-share DAX index breached the elusive 3,000-point level for the first time ever on Friday but champagne celebrations quickly turned to caution as dealers experienced a touch of vertigo at such dizzy heights.
The main factor spurring the market to new peaks was a 30-month record high for the dollar, trading above 1.61 marks -- good news for the many German firms which have a strong export performance.
A further boost came from the expiry of DAX options.
The index, which topped the long-targeted 3,000-point threshold in pre-bourse IBIS electronic business, ended bourse trade at 3,001.37, up 8.06 points but off an earlier lifetime high of 3,011.17.
The market lost some more of its earlier sparkle by late afternoon electronic trade with the IBIS DAX around 3,004.
Dealers had been seeking all week to push the DAX above 3,000 but had failed repeatedly despite coming within two points on Thursday.
Market players had spoken of bottles of champagne hidden away for when the market hit the "magic" 3,000. While this level has limited technical implications, it provides a psychological boost.
Once the DAX reached the target, however, caution took over. The market was unable to capitalise on the positive environment and was held back from further gains, chiefly by low volumes.
Dealers said there was also a lack of fresh market-moving data to lift the index to more significant heights.
"Of course we are happy to see the 3,000 mark but it doesn't mean the start of anything big," said one Frankfurt dealer.
Another said he needed more convincing that the trend was genuine and added that reaching 3,030 points would be more conclusive.
Indeed, some traders seemed to fear that reaching 3,000 could signal the end of the bull market altogether, adding that the atmosphere on the floor of the bourse was more muted than ecstatic.
"There's no reason to celebrate, really. We've a long year ahead of us," said one dealer, adding that 3,000 points was just another number.

A trader at another Frankfurt bank commented: "It's more dangerous in a way if champagne corks start popping. If we get too much euphoria in the market, we could see the peak turn around quickly and start to fall, just like in the 1980s.
"We're worried that the options expiry might have pushed the DAX artificially higher and that we could see some form of consolidation now," the trader added.
